title: Compare and Contrast Cloud Deployment Models

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: A cloud deployment model describes where the cloud environment exists, who uses it, and how much control the organization has over it.
CompTIA wants you to recognize four models: public, private, hybrid, and community.
The main question is not simply, 'Is this in the cloud?' The better question is: Who owns or uses the environment, and does the organization need dedicated control or shared resources?

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Who needs access to this cloud environment, and how dedicated does the infrastructure need to be?
sections.callout: Shared provider environment → public. Dedicated organization environment → private. Combination → hybrid. Shared by organizations with common needs → community.

sections.title: Public Cloud
paragraphs: A public cloud is operated by a cloud provider and delivers services to customers using the provider's infrastructure.
Different customers can use the provider's cloud while their environments remain logically separated.
Organizations choose public cloud when they want rapid access to cloud resources, less physical infrastructure to maintain, provider-managed facilities, and flexible resource usage.
Think: Use the cloud provider's environment instead of owning the whole facility.
sections.callout: If a business consumes cloud resources from a provider's shared cloud infrastructure → think public cloud.

sections.title: Private Cloud
paragraphs: A private cloud is dedicated to a single organization.
The organization receives greater control because the infrastructure is not provided as a general shared environment for unrelated customers.
Private cloud may be useful when an organization has demanding security, control, compliance, or customization requirements.
Think: Cloud capabilities, but dedicated to us.
sections.callout: If one organization needs a dedicated cloud environment → think private cloud.

sections.title: On-Premises Private Cloud
paragraphs: A private cloud can operate on premises, meaning the infrastructure remains within facilities controlled by the organization.
This provides cloud-style capabilities while the organization retains direct responsibility for its physical environment.
Think: Our cloud, in our building.
sections.callout: If cloud infrastructure is dedicated to one organization and physically maintained at its own site → think on-premises private cloud.

sections.title: Hybrid Cloud
paragraphs: A hybrid cloud combines different environments, commonly private infrastructure and public cloud resources.
Applications or data can use the environment that best matches their requirements.
For example, an organization may keep sensitive workloads in a private environment while using public cloud resources for other applications.
Think: Part ours, part provider.
sections.callout: If the solution combines private or on-premises resources with public cloud resources → think hybrid cloud.

sections.title: Community Cloud
paragraphs: A community cloud is shared by multiple organizations that have similar requirements or interests.
Those organizations may share security requirements, regulatory requirements, business missions, or industry needs.
Think: A private club for organizations with something important in common.
sections.callout: If several organizations with shared requirements use the same cloud environment → think community cloud.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Dedicated cloud for one business → Private
Organization owns and operates its private cloud locally → On-premises private
Public cloud plus private or on-premises environment → Hybrid
Several organizations share similar compliance or mission requirements → Community

entries.title: Public vs. Community
paragraphs: Both can involve multiple organizations. Public cloud is broadly offered by a provider; community cloud is intended for a defined group with common requirements.

entries.title: Private vs. On Premises
paragraphs: Private describes who the cloud is dedicated to. On premises describes where the infrastructure resides.
Dedicated cloud infrastructure inside the organization's own facility points strongly toward on-premises private cloud.

entries.title: Hybrid Does Not Mean Multicloud
paragraphs: For this objective, hybrid combines different deployment environments, such as private infrastructure with public cloud.
Do not automatically choose hybrid just because more than one cloud service appears in the scenario.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Provider cloud available to customers → Public cloud
Dedicated to one organization → Private cloud
Dedicated cloud inside the company's own facility → On-premises private cloud
Private or on-premises plus public cloud → Hybrid cloud
Organizations with shared requirements use one environment → Community cloud
